subject: pathology
title: Carcinoid Tumours, Pancoast Tumour, Horner and SVC Syndromes, Lambert-Eaton, and Hamartoma

steps.tx: Bronchial carcinoid tumours grow as vascular central polyps causing wheeze, haemoptysis, and recurrent pneumonia, typical forms rarely metastasising, atypical forms by mitoses and necrosis behaving worse. Salt and pepper neuroendocrine chromatin marks the **bronchial carcinoid tumour, typical versus atypical**. Typical tumours show fewer than 2 mitoses per 2 square millimetres and no necrosis, whereas atypical tumours show 2 to 10 mitoses or punctate necrosis.
steps.say: A vascular bronchial polyp with wheeze and haemoptysis in a younger non smoker suggests carcinoid.

left.title: Typical carcinoid
points: Carcinoid syndrome rare from lung primary

steps.tx: At bronchoscopy this tumour announces itself as a smooth, cherry red polyp that bleeds readily when the scope brushes past it. The inset explains that vascular look: nests of uniform neuroendocrine cells whose nuclei show finely speckled **salt and pepper chromatin**. Because the lesion sits centrally, patients often arrive with wheeze treated as asthma, one sided pneumonia that keeps returning, or streaky haemoptysis. A biopsy can bleed briskly, so the bronchoscopist warns the team before sampling such a polyp.
steps.say: A bleeding central bronchial polyp with salt and pepper chromatin is the classic face of bronchial carcinoid.

steps.tx: Carcinoid syndrome flushes and diarrhoeas when serotonin reaches systemic circulation, usually from liver metastases of gut primaries, while bronchial primaries occasionally bypass hepatic inactivation directly. The mediator remains **serotonin driven carcinoid syndrome**. Urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid above the reference range confirms excess serotonin breakdown, and right sided valve fibrosis can follow years of such exposure.
steps.say: Bronchial carcinoids can flush without liver metastases because their serotonin skips the portal filter.

steps.tx: Pancoast tumours invade the superior sulcus, destroying first ribs and vertebrae, injuring brachial plexus lower trunk and sympathetic chain, producing shoulder pain radiating down ulnar arm. The apical invader is **Pancoast (superior sulcus) tumour syndrome**. Imaging that maps rib destruction, plus magnetic resonance views of the brachial plexus, decides whether chemoradiation should precede attempted resection.
steps.say: Shoulder pain down the ulnar arm with an apical mass is Pancoast tumour until imaging acquits it.

vis.caption: Lung carcinoma patterns including apical superior sulcus tumours.

steps.tx: Horner syndrome joins Pancoast anatomy when stellate ganglion invasion interrupts sympathetic supply, producing ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis, and enophthalmos on the tumour's side. That sympathetic signature is **Horner syndrome of superior sulcus invasion**. Pharmacological pupil testing can support the finding, although urgent apical imaging matters far more than proving the pupil signs at the bedside.
steps.say: Ptosis, small pupil, dry face beside shoulder pain localises invasion to the stellate ganglion.

steps.tx: Superior vena cava syndrome swells face, neck, and arms with venous collaterals when malignancy, increasingly lymphoma and lung cancer, compresses or thromboses the great vein, stenting relieving emergencies. The venous emergency is **superior vena cava (SVC) syndrome**. Endovascular stenting can ease severe breathlessness within days, yet obtaining tissue still determines which definitive cancer treatment follows.
steps.say: Swollen face, distended neck veins, and a mediastinal mass mean SVC syndrome; tissue and stent race together.

steps.tx: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome weakens proximal muscles through presynaptic calcium channel antibodies, improving transiently with activity, drying mouth, and betraying small cell cancer in half its patients. The presynaptic syndrome is **Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS)**. Antibodies target P/Q type voltage gated calcium channels at the presynaptic terminal, and 3,4-diaminopyridine boosts acetylcholine release from surviving endings.
steps.say: Weakness that briefly improves with use plus dry mouth means Lambert-Eaton; hunt small cell cancer.

steps.tx: Pulmonary hamartoma, commonest benign lung tumour, grows coin lesions of cartilage, fat, and cleft epithelium with popcorn calcification in middle aged incidental imaging. The benign coin is **pulmonary hamartoma (chondroid hamartoma)**. Cartilage lobules with entrapped respiratory epithelium and flecks of fat explain why these benign nodules enlarge only slowly over many years.
steps.say: Popcorn calcification in a coin lesion reassures toward hamartoma, lung's commonest benign tumour.

steps.tx: Metastatic lung disease outnumbers primary tumours, cannonball deposits from kidney, testis, and colon, lymphangitic threads from breast and stomach, and miliary patterns each narrating their primaries. Pattern reading performs **metastatic patterns in the lung**. Renal cell carcinoma classically seeds cannonball deposits, whereas breast and gastric primaries thread tumour along pulmonary lymphatics instead.
steps.say: Cannonballs, lymphangitic threads, or miliary seeds in lung each point back to a different primary.
